chunk_map.heading: Take the ranked ten, leave the rest on disk
Phase 1: Run the curated skill on your feature and save the map
Point the skill at your feature
Kick off the pass, then work the other window
Phase 2: Read the map back before you decide the delta
Phase 3: Add the surface the skill over-called, and the one it missed
Push back until the reason names your codebase
Phase 4: Add the context header a cold reader needs

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest calls, both hold: chunk 7 "Push back until the reason names your codebase" line 82 "Push back until the reason names something specific to your codebase" — "the reason" continues chunk 6's "a one-line reason each" (line 70), immediate-continuation carve-out, adjacent chunk. Chunk 8 line 88 "You're about to hand this map to the STRIDE skill" — STRIDE named in the lede (line 11, chunk 0), arc-earned spine vocabulary reused across slides. Chunk 1's opener (lines 17-20) previews "the saved map"/"the file" before Phase 1 runs the skill, but this is the deliberately-kept overview beat the maintainer block names "The selective-reading opener chunk" (line 105 maintainer) — preview framing, not a claim the referent already exists.

Cross-file references are named, not positional: line 47 "The plan path you noted at Module 2's close" (named by module, not "the earlier module said"); line 52 "start *Author your test-strategy skill* there" (named by title). No "the opening lecture said" style positional callback anywhere in the file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -rn "plan.*close\|plan file path" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/*.md -> earn-the-trust.md L770: "Note the plan file path on your way out: M3 reads it" and the arc glossary row "Plan mode displays the path inline when it writes; the student notes it at module close for M3" (L870) confirm line 47's "plan path you noted at Module 2's close" resolves against a real M2 beat. Also: the diff at line 94 fixed a stranded reference in this exact rule's lane — "If you rushed Phase 2" (pre-324b81d7) corrected to "If you rushed Phase 3", now pointing at the phase that actually does the delta work.

Closest call: chunk 7 "Push back until the reason names your codebase" is a single bullet (lines 82-83) but carries a self-standing claim plus a concrete worked contrast ("The billing webhook re-hits the queue on retry..." vs "webhooks need auth") — not a wait-state or context-dependent fragment.

Checked all 9 headers against their chunk content under cover-the-body/uncover test; each matches (e.g. chunk 6 "Phase 3: Add the surface the skill over-called, and the one it missed" / lines 65-66 name exactly the over-call and the miss). No header the chunk's own content contradicts.

No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction anywhere. No anaphora/epistrophe triples. No self-grading superlative (closest non-violating phrase: line 27 "the breadth walk", reused descriptively, not self-grading). No number-with-retraction. No abstraction-noun stack surviving concreteness ask ("the two-window move" line 51 names a concrete mechanic, not an abstraction, and is separately accept-noted). No empty-leg verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "surface" throughout (lines 7, 9, 18, 65-66, etc.) is the security-domain term (access surface, attack surface), not repo dialect ("writing surface" as noun) — explicitly carved out by §8. No forcing function / compendium / firing / beat / mood / Connections found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only two non-chrome bolds in the file: chunk 6 (Phase 3) carries **The over-call.** and **The miss.** (lines 65, 66), a two-item delta menu — matches the reading-list/menu exception (each entry may carry one handle, ≤1-per-slide budget off) and is directly attested in the maintainer block's own Emphasis note (line ~130 expanded: "the delta menu pair **The over-call.** / **The miss.**"). The on-screen **User** label (line 33) is likewise attested there. All other bold in the file (**Time:**, **Window:**, **What you do:**, **What you build:**, **The point:**, **What happened:**) is widget chrome, exempted by the same note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Whole file is a single exercise body under one `.phase--exercise` wrapper when included in a module (curriculum/exercises/*.md), no phase-less top-level prose section sits outside that wrapper — unlike the prework/supplementary/reference case §10 warns about. No structural markup changed in the pinned diff.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js` -> "OK — 59 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent." (exit 0). Phase 1-4 headers consecutive; the in-file "Phase 3" reference (line 94) resolves in-file.

rules_evaluated.evidence: `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js` -> "OK — 59 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut." (exit 0). No "below/above/at the top of this page" pointers found in a manual read either.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/map-the-access-surface.md` -> "slides: 9  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets  oversized: 0" — every slide within limits (exit 0).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 9 headers are imperative ("Take the ranked ten...", "Point the skill at your feature", "Push back until the reason names your codebase") or Phase-label ("Phase 1: ..." through "Phase 4: ...") except "What this sets up", which is an orientation-style closer heading (carve-out class, cf. "You are here") — no declarative-claim header exists to check literal truth against, so §15's claim-requirement never engages here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked candidates against the three classes: line 18 ("The countermove from M1 goes to work...") functions, tying the M1 technique to why output routes to disk — not bare doctrine restatement. Line 39 ("These are the moves Claude has on hand...") sets up the lazy-load teaching the next line leans on, per the maintainer's own 'Skill-introspection...kept, not cut' note — not self-referential design commentary. Chunk 9's closer (lines 93-95) is explicitly accept-noted: "Carded and kept (Antti 2026-08-25): the *What this sets up* slide — the sow-here-reap-at-STRIDE motivation stays; do not re-card." No un-accept-noted doctrine-restatement, design-commentary, or kicker bullet found.

notes: Rules 15, 16 and 17 postdate the rule-7/blocking partition list in check_slides.md and are not named in either its blocking or non-blocking enumeration (same gap the compendium itself flags for rules 9-14). Applied the stated principle (blocking = cannot be understood/trusted as shown; non-blocking = polish on a working slide) to classify all three as non-blocking — a wrong heading mood, a low-value bullet, or a stale retitle-leftover reads as house-style/clutter, not comprehension failure. Rules 4 and 13 are out of scope per the prefill sidecar (shape hash 1b7965156c82fee5) and are not rowed here; see prefill-instance.js --merge.
